The dome's live predictions page now carries a second formulation aimed directly at this WIN: 'FSF Formula — LOCKED 2026-03-22 (WIN-044): The Field Strength Factor for all 9 stations is now independently derived from V12 geometry: FSF(lat) = 0.19550 / sin(lat)0.1640 × 32.974(lat/90) [RMSE = 0.0071 across all 9 stations]'. Four observations close this escape hatch. First, the formula's only input is geographic latitude — a globe coordinate with no dome-native meaning; disc radius, firmament height, and every other dome parameter are absent from it. Second, 'independently derived' is contradicted by the formula's own annotation: derivations carry proofs, fits carry goodness-of-fit statistics, and '[RMSE = 0.0071 across all 9 stations]' is fit-language measured against the nine values the formula allegedly derives. Third, its three constants (0.19550, 0.1640, 32.974) appear nowhere else on the dome site and have no published derivation path from any dome parameter — they are three free knobs, catalogued as FORM-V51-005 in our formula audit (Section 4.2). Fourth, the lock date is unverifiable in the public record: predictions.html has exactly one commit in its git history (571373e, 2026-04-05, 'V51.1 Rigor & Audit'), and the 2026-03-12 snapshot of the page lacks the paragraph — the 'LOCKED' label lives on the mutable side of the repository, the same wrong-side-anchoring pattern documented in the Timestamp Error tab. The replacement formula is also a worse fit than the identity it obscures: plain tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) lands closer to the published values than the three-knob FSF(lat) at five of the seven stations with published FSF (e.g., HAD: identity −0.0001 vs formula +0.006). Far from rescuing the V12-derivation claim, the locked formula completes the self-contradiction: asked to defend a formula whose output depends on dome version, the dome published one containing no dome variables at all.
